bugs.description: Keyless writer (Stage 3) exhausts its cumulative budget across retries and produces no article. A live keyless run of src.agent_sdk.pipeline hit BudgetExceededError (cap=$0.2169, cost_at_abort=$0.3166) after ~9 min with output/posts/ empty. The cumulative-budget-across-attempts logic plus repeated writer regeneration (_WRITER_MAX_ATTEMPTS) burned the budget, implying the writer is looping on malformed output rather than the budget merely being too low. DIAGNOSTIC PENDING: rerun with a generous --writer-budget to distinguish under-budget vs malformed-output loop. Related to the preamble/code-fence recovery in the closed PR #441 (_extract_article) and BUG-044.
bugs.root_cause_notes: DIAGNOSED (generous --writer-budget 3.00 run): DUAL cause. (1) Under-budget — the run completed at $0.5907 total, but the defaults (run_pipeline writer 0.30 / CLI 0.60) are exhausted once the writer retries. (2) The writer emits conversational preamble on some attempts (e.g. 'The search tool is wired to arXiv... I'll write the article grounded in...'), failing the well-formed check (starts_with_dash=False) and forcing a retry that burns budget. Fix: port the closed PR #441 _extract_article preamble/fence recovery into the stage3 retry loop so preamble attempts recover in-place instead of retrying, AND raise the default writer budget for margin. NOTE: a generous-budget run DID produce a publish-valid article (publication_validator PASSED) — keyless generation works.
bugs.discovered_by: B-009 T1 fail-fast keyless run
bugs.fix_notes: _extract_article preamble recovery wired into the Stage 3 retry loop; verified end-to-end by the B-010 claude_web acceptance run (clean completion, no malformed-retry budget burn).

bugs.description: Async-generator cleanup bug masks BudgetExceededError. When _raise_if_budget_exceeded fires inside _collect_text (stage3_runner.py:381->335), a 'RuntimeError: aclose(): asynchronous generator is already running' is raised during handling of the BudgetExceededError, so the clean typed budget error is obscured by an async cleanup RuntimeError. The query() async generator is not closed cleanly on the early raise.
bugs.root_cause_notes: Raising out of the `async for message in query(...)` loop without closing/awaiting the async generator triggers aclose() while it is still running. Needs structured cleanup (e.g. break + explicit aclose, or aclosing()).
bugs.discovered_by: B-009 T1 fail-fast keyless run
bugs.fix_notes: break-then-raise so BudgetExceededError surfaces cleanly; contract-tested (a mock cannot reproduce the real-SDK 'already running' RuntimeError, but the raise-mid-iteration that triggers it is removed).

bugs.description: arXiv search-term optimizer garbles words. _optimize_search_terms (scripts/arxiv_search.py:302) lowercases the query then substring-replaces mapping keys with no word boundaries, so 'AI'->'artificial intelligence OR machine learning' fires inside 'drain' -> 'dr artificial intelligence OR machine learning n'. Observed live: query 'why flaky tests quietly drain engineering budgets' became '...quietly drartificial intelligence OR machine learningn engineering budgets', producing junk arXiv queries that return nothing.
bugs.root_cause_notes: Naive str.replace() of term-mapping keys; needs word-boundary (\b) matching.

bugs.description: Keyless deterministic research is unreliable and aborts the whole pipeline. The two free providers (arXiv, Semantic Scholar) rate-limit/err heavily (HTTP 429/503); when BOTH fail on a topic, deterministic research returns zero sources and the empty-research guard (#438) aborts the run (exit 2, 'Pipeline aborted: research failed', provider_failed={'arxiv':True,'semantic_scholar':True}). Observed live: a default-budget keyless run aborted before the writer. This is the primary blocker to reliable keyless article production — bigger than the writer bugs. Likely mitigation: default the keyless path to research_mode='claude_web' (ADR-0013, Claude's own WebSearch on the subscription — not the rate-limited academic APIs), which is exactly why claude_web was introduced.
bugs.root_cause_notes: Keyless research depends on free rate-limited APIs with an abort-on-empty guard. Decide the reliable keyless research mode (claude_web vs hardened deterministic) — affects B-010's canonical-command choice and the live-run acceptance gate.
bugs.discovered_by: B-010 T1 validation run
bugs.fix_notes: Mitigated by defaulting the keyless path to research_mode=claude_web (documented canonical in the runbook). Verified: claude_web produced a publish-valid article on the exact topic that aborted under deterministic. deterministic remains rate-limited; claude_web is the reliable keyless research mode.

This blog has remote_theme COMMENTED OUT and uses local layouts (default/page/post) — there is no `single` layout, so the parent layout silently did not apply and the draft rendered as bare markdown-to-HTML. bugs.description: OWNER-REPORTED (visual). The owner wants Claude's own visualization capability to produce the HERO IMAGE and ALL charts/images a post requires. Today the pipeline only (a) draws a single data chart via chart_renderer.py (matplotlib) and (b) emits a hero-image PROMPT sidecar for a human to render elsewhere. Desired: end-to-end Claude-generated visuals so a post ships with its hero + any supporting figures without a manual image step.
bugs.component: src/agent_sdk (graphics stage) + image_prompt_synth + deploy hero-image handoff
bugs.root_cause_notes: CONSTRAINT CONFLICT — must be resolved by the owner before any fix. CLAUDE.md constraint #4 (NON-NEGOTIABLE) currently forbids pipeline hero-image generation of ANY kind — not DALL-E/Gemini (needs a keyed service, violates constraint #1), and explicitly 'not procedural/PIL image generation either'; the hero is human-supplied from a prompt. So this request REVERSES documented policy. Feasible keyless interpretations to consider: (i) charts — already allowed & keyless (code-drawn), extend coverage to multiple figures per post; (ii) hero as a CODE/SVG-drawn editorial illustration authored by Claude (keyless, but currently banned by #4's 'no procedural' clause); (iii) true raster AI hero art — needs an image model = a keyed/paid service = blocked by constraints #1/#2 unless the owner adds one. NEXT STEP: owner decides whether to amend constraint #4 and which interpretation is in scope, then spec it (spec-driven-development).
bugs.discovered_by: owner report
bugs.resolution: B-016a: constraint #4 amended to allow code-drawn visuals (SVG hero + matplotlib charts); raster/pixel models still forbidden. Hero copying wired into deploy() and deploy_review() (was never wired). Verified live on draft ...-f40e8d27.

bugs.description: OWNER-REPORTED (prose). The generated flaky-tests article ('Green Light, Red Ledger…') reads like AI slop despite passing the deterministic economist-writing gates. It CLEARS the mechanical checks (named companies: Atlassian/Google/Microsoft/CloudBees; <=4 headings; colon-twist title; data-dense; no lists) yet still exhibits AI tells the current Stage-4 banned-phrase list does not catch.
bugs.component: src/agent_sdk._shared (Stage 4 polish / banned-phrase list) + skills/economist-writing enforcement
bugs.root_cause_notes: Concrete AI-slop tells found on review against skills/economist-writing (none are in the current deterministic banlist): (1) EM-DASH rhythm — em-dashes used as the default connective, often 1-2 per paragraph. (2) META-COMMENTARY on its own argument: 'The argument here is blunter than most engineering post-mortems allow'; 'The numbers, once examined, make this case almost without assistance'; 'The most interesting question is not whether flaky tests are expensive… it is why'. (3) 'NOT X BUT Y' antithesis scaffold repeated ~6x: 'not cutting corners—she is making a…decision', 'not a nuisance …but a quantifiable payroll cost', 'not defective code but tests', 'not merely expensive but epistemically impossible'. (4) UNFALSIFIABLE SUPERLATIVES / overreach: 'No other category of engineering waste operates so openly and at such scale with so little executive scrutiny.' (5) PURPLE / MIXED-METAPHOR pile-up: dripping tap -> flooding basement -> 'the plumber charges considerably more than the pipe was worth'; 'offloaded from the pipeline to the engineer's nervous system'; 'the engineer is hunting a ghost'; 'auto-retry is an anaesthetic, not a cure'. (6) FAUX-SPECIFIC cuteness: 'a test decided to behave differently on a Tuesday'. These pass because Stage 4 only strips a fixed hedging/closing set; the rhythmic + rhetorical AI tells are unlisted.
bugs.discovered_by: owner report + economist-writing skill review
bugs.fix_notes: Candidate fixes (spec first): extend the deterministic banlist / add heuristics for em-dash density, 'not X but Y' frequency, meta-commentary stems ('the argument here', 'the numbers…make this case'), and superlative overreach; and/or add an economist-writing Stage-4 judge pass that flags these. Add regression fixtures built from the tells above.
bugs.resolution: B-017: four flag-only detectors (em_dash_density, antithesis_scaffold, meta_commentary, unfalsifiable_superlative) added to publication_validator.py; HIGH/MEDIUM never CRITICAL. Verified on the real article. Metaphor tell (#5) is semantic - parked, not faked. Spec: docs/specs/B-017-ai-slop-enforcement.md

bugs.title: Empty image: "" frontmatter fails the blog's required build check (html-proofer)
bugs.description: Stage 4 stamped image: "" into every article (_shared._DEFAULT_IMAGE). Our validator reads empty and absent identically (chart-only mode) so it passed locally, but Jekyll does not: in Liquid only nil/false are falsy, so "" satisfies the blog post layout guard {% if page.image %}, responsive-image.html renders an with no usable src, and html-proofer fails with "image has no src or srcset attribute". This fails oviney/blog REQUIRED build check.
bugs.evidence: oviney/blog PR #1159 build FAIL (run 30086689055): html-proofer 1 failure at _site/review/green-light-red-ledger-...-1530b611/index.html:166 "image has no src or srcset attribute". Draft frontmatter line 8 is image: "". PR #1157 build PASSED because review.html then extended a nonexistent layout and rendered bare (no img tag emitted).
bugs.root_cause: _shared._DEFAULT_IMAGE = "" injected whenever finalize ran without a hero. The stale comment claimed the frontmatter schema requires the key present; schema_validator requires only layout/title/date/categories.
bugs.resolution: Removed the injection and strip any empty image: line (_EMPTY_IMAGE_LINE) so chart-only articles OMIT the key. Regression: TestEmptyImageFrontmatterNeverEmitted in tests/test_stage4_editorial_fixes.py. Hero images stay human-supplied (constraint #4).
bugs.impact: Blocked the main publishing path, not just B-013 review drafts: every generated article PR would fail the blog required build check once it carried image: "".
bugs.verification: Fresh draft ...-a7014d4d deployed with NO image: key; blog build passes; leak test 10/10 incl. no src-less . Local CRITICAL empty_image_value guard added.

bugs.title: Flaky-tests article shipped a broken chart: 5 of 6 bars invisible, raw count labelled as %
bugs.description: The chart embedded in the flaky-tests article plotted percentages (84, 21, 2.5, 1.3, 1.1) on the same linear axis as a raw count of 150000 developer-hours. The count dwarfed everything so all five percentage bars rendered as zero-width, and the count was labelled "150000 %" - a unit that is flatly wrong.
bugs.root_cause: Stale artifact: the PNG was rendered 2026-07-21, before B-014 added the mixed-unit guard (_MAX_VALUE_SPAN) on 2026-07-22. Nothing re-rendered or re-validated the existing chart afterwards.
bugs.resolution: Confirmed the B-014 guard now rejects the original spec (150000 vs 1.1). Re-rendered on one coherent measure: share of failing builds caused by flaky tests vs genuine defects (Google 84/16, Jira Frontend 21/79), matching what the prose promises the chart shows.
bugs.impact: Would have published a chart conveying no information and stating a false unit. Charts predating B-014 are not automatically re-validated - a gap worth watching on older articles.

bugs.title: Pipeline never emitted tags: every published article fails the blog validate-editorial gate
bugs.description: oviney/blog scripts/validate-posts.sh requires a tags field with at least 2 tags in inline bracket format, all lowercase-hyphen; an uppercase character is a hard error. The pipeline never emitted tags at all, so the first real generated article to reach _posts failed validate-editorial on blog main.
bugs.evidence: Test Jekyll Build run 30138114457 on oviney/blog main: green-light-red-ledger... missing required front-matter field: tags. validate-posts: FAILED.
bugs.root_cause: Our frontmatter contract (_shared.apply_editorial_fixes + frontmatter_schema) was written against our OWN validator, which never required tags. The blog gate was never exercised on a real generated article: B-015 measured the gate matrix on a layout PR, not on an article.
bugs.resolution: _derive_tags kebab-cases the categories into a tags line, topped up from _FALLBACK_TAGS so the 2-tag floor holds for a single-category article. Verified by running the blog OWN scripts/validate-posts.sh: PASSED. Live post hotfixed separately. Regression: TestTagsAlwaysEmitted, 4 tests.
bugs.impact: Blocked publication of every article at the blog gate. Also surfaced that validate-posts.sh requires image: too, so a chart-only article that omits image: per BUG-055 would ALSO fail this gate. Currently masked because B-016 always draws a hero. Tracked in B-015.

bugs.title: Six tests in test_economist_agent.py made live arXiv/citation HTTP calls; the merge gate's runtime was set by a third party's rate limiter
bugs.description: TestRunResearchAgent and TestIntegration patched agents.research_agent.call_llm but not the TWO other network paths inside ResearchAgent.research: _gather_arxiv_research (live arXiv HTTP) and scripts.citation_verifier.verify_citations (fetches every citation URL).
bugs.evidence: pytest --durations on the file: 34 passed in 624.53s (10m24s), with six tests accounting for 620s (127.75/127.24/122.40/97.14/96.21/50.21). Log shows 'arXiv transient error (HTTP 429 ...); retry 2/3 after 1.5s'. Reproduced on a clean tree via git stash, so it predates B-019.
bugs.root_cause: Incomplete mocking at the wrong boundary. The tests were written against the LLM seam; the arXiv provider and citation verifier are reached deeper inside ResearchAgent.research and were never stubbed. Because the production code catches network errors and retries with backoff, the tests still PASSED — the defect was invisible except as duration, which is why it survived so long.
bugs.impact: Severity raised MEDIUM -> HIGH on measurement. Cost is not a fixed ~2 min as first assessed: arXiv rate-limits under repeated runs, so the gate got slower the more it was used and was unbounded. make ci-local is the only merge gate (ADR-0015); it also failed offline and depended on arXiv availability.
bugs.proposed_fix: Patch ResearchAgent._gather_arxiv_research in the TestRunResearchAgent fixture to return an empty insights dict. Add a suite-wide guard test that fails if any test opens a socket.
bugs.resolution: Two layers. (1) tests/_netguard.py + an autouse _no_network fixture block all non-loopback sockets, so no test can reach a third party; opt out with @pytest.mark.allow_network. Loopback still works for local servers/IPC. (2) An autouse fixture in test_economist_agent.py stubs both paths at source, removing the retry backoff the guard alone left behind. The exception lives in tests/_netguard.py, not conftest.py, so it has one module identity (conftest is imported as top-level 'conftest', so 'from tests.conftest import ...' yields a different class and pytest.raises silently fails to match). Regression: tests/test_no_network_guard.py, 6 tests.

bugs.title: _collect_text has no wall-clock timeout, so any Stage 3 LLM call can hang the pipeline indefinitely
bugs.description: src/agent_sdk/stage3_runner.py::_collect_text awaits the Agent SDK query() generator with no asyncio timeout. max_budget_usd bounds COST but not TIME, and a stalled or very long generation blocks forever with no output.
bugs.evidence: Found building B-016b: the first real hero generation ran 15 minutes and produced no SVG and no log line beyond CLI startup (exit 124 from the outer `timeout`). Bisected with probes: a trivial prompt returns in 4.7s and a small SVG ask in 19.3s, but a composed-scene drawing request had not returned at 205s. Nothing in _collect_text would ever have stopped it.
bugs.root_cause: Missing timeout. The writer and graphics agents are bounded on cost (max_budget_usd) but not on wall clock, so the same exposure exists for every Stage 3 call, not just the hero.
bugs.impact: A hung provider call stalls the whole pipeline with no diagnostic. The operator sees no output and cannot tell a slow run from a dead one. Affects the writer and graphics agents too.
bugs.proposed_fix: Give _collect_text an explicit timeout_s parameter with a sane default and wrap the query() iteration in asyncio.wait_for, raising a typed AgentCallTimeout that callers can treat as a retryable attempt failure. B-016b already bounds its OWN calls (240s draw / 120s critique) as a local mitigation; this generalises it.
bugs.workaround: B-016b's hero calls are individually bounded; other callers are not.
bugs.fix_notes: Every SDK collector now runs under asyncio.timeout and converts expiry into a typed ModelCallTimeoutError labelled with the call ("writer (attempt 2/3)"). Scope widened past the logged component: research/_llm.py and research/claude_web.py had the identical unbounded async-for, and research is the longest leg. Bounds from measured data: 900s per Stage 3 call, 300s per research orchestration call, 900s for the web-research leg. A timeout fails fast rather than being retried; research keeps its existing soft degrade to an empty brief. hero_author already bounded itself at 600s and was left alone.

bugs.title: image_gate.py is DALL-E-era PNG-only and is dead code on the keyless hero path
bugs.description: src/agent_sdk/image_gate.py checks PNG magic bytes, 1792x1024 +/-5%, and a 50 KB floor. Heroes are now SVG (Operating Constraint #4), so none of those checks can apply. B-016b added hero_svg.check_hero_svg instead of contorting it.
bugs.evidence: Noted while building B-016b; image_gate is still imported by pipeline for the --resume handshake path.
bugs.root_cause: Left behind by the DALL-E retirement (ADR-0014 / B-009). The handshake path that uses it predates SVG heroes.
bugs.impact: Misleading rather than broken: a reader of the code may believe hero images are gated on PNG dimensions. Also constrains the --resume handshake to PNG drops.
bugs.proposed_fix: Decide the fate of the --resume image handshake now that Stage 3 draws the hero. If the handshake stays, teach it check_hero_svg for .svg drops; if it goes, delete image_gate.py with it. Spec-worthy, not a patch — it is on a user-facing path.
bugs.fix_notes: Resolved by deletion (owner call, B-021 slice 3). image_gate.py was only reachable from the --resume handshake, which existed to receive raster art that Operating Constraint #4 forbids and B-016b made unnecessary. Removed the module, --image-mode/--resume/--no-image, the handshake + state machinery, and exit codes 10/11 (retired, not reused). One path remains.
bugs.verification: 9 regression tests + full suite 2377 passed, make ci-local green (2026-07-28)

bugs.title: Default --writer-budget $0.60 cannot absorb a single writer retry, so the default invocation aborts
bugs.description: The writer budget is consumed ACROSS retry attempts, not per attempt: each attempt is given the remaining balance. One Sonnet writer attempt costs ~$0.42, so a first attempt that produces malformed output (a normal, handled condition with _WRITER_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3) leaves too little for the second, which then aborts the whole pipeline with BudgetExceededError.
bugs.evidence: B-020 acceptance run, 2026-07-27, default budgets: 'Writer attempt 1/3 produced malformed output (starts_with_dash=True, body_empty=True); retrying' then 'BudgetExceededError: cap=$0.3352, cost_at_abort=$0.4216'. $0.3352 is $0.60 minus the ~$0.26 the malformed attempt already spent. Pipeline exited 1 after ~14 min with no article.
bugs.root_cause: The default was never validated against a real retry. Its own help text claims it is 'sized for Sonnet with retries + tool turns', but at ~$0.42 per attempt three attempts need ~$1.26 and even two need ~$0.85.
bugs.impact: The DEFAULT invocation fails whenever the writer's first attempt is malformed — which happened on the very first real end-to-end run. Wastes ~14 minutes and the cost of the attempts, and produces no article. The retry mechanism that exists to add resilience instead guarantees failure.
bugs.proposed_fix: Raise the default to ~$1.60 (3 attempts x $0.42 plus headroom) and correct the help text with the measured per-attempt cost. Consider giving each attempt its own cap rather than sharing one balance, so a wasted attempt cannot starve the retry it exists to enable. Verify by running with the default and forcing a retry.
bugs.fix_notes: The cumulative cap was correct; the DEFAULT was incoherent with _WRITER_MAX_ATTEMPTS. Default now derives from _WRITER_ATTEMPT_COST_USD (0.45, measured) x _WRITER_MAX_ATTEMPTS, shared by run_stage3/run_pipeline/--writer-budget. An unfundable retry is refused BEFORE dispatch with an error naming the flag and the arithmetic, instead of the SDK generic abort.

bugs.title: Wiring the hero into Stage 3 made `make ci-local` issue real LLM calls; the gate began timing out
bugs.description: hero_author holds its OWN reference to _collect_text. The ~10 test files that patch stage3_runner._collect_text therefore did not cover the hero step, which called the real Agent SDK during the test suite.
bugs.evidence: output/posts/test.image_prompt.md and output/posts/images/test-hero.svg appeared in the repo during a gate run, containing REAL generated content built from a test fixture's frontmatter ('Subject: alt', 'Editorial framing: cap'). Decisive measurement: the gate timed out at 900s (EXIT=124) before the guard and ran in 119.05s with 2371 passed after it.
bugs.root_cause: Introduced by me in B-016b. The BUG-058 socket guard cannot see these calls: claude_agent_sdk.query spawns a subprocess CLI, so no in-process socket opens.
bugs.impact: Every make ci-local made live subscription calls (~$0.45 and ~450s each) and wrote generated artefacts into output/. The gate became unusable — it timed out — which would have pushed people to skip it, the exact failure that let BUG-055..057 reach main.
bugs.resolution: netguard.install_model_guard patches stage3_runner.query — the single chokepoint every model call funnels through — as an autouse fixture with the @pytest.mark.allow_network opt-out. Tests that legitimately exercise _collect_text internals patch it themselves and their patch wins. Regression: 3 tests in test_no_network_guard.py, one specifically covering the separate-reference trap. Zero existing tests broke, confirming none were relying on the real SDK.

bugs.title: The graphics agent has no retry, so one malformed chart spec kills the pipeline after the writer has already succeeded
bugs.description: run_stage3 calls the graphics agent once and passes the result straight to render_chart, whose failures are fatal by design (a missing chart leaves a broken body embed). The writer gets _WRITER_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 for exactly the same class of malformed-LLM-output problem; graphics gets one attempt.
bugs.evidence: B-020 acceptance run 3, 2026-07-27: 'ChartRenderError: spec.data is required and must be a non-empty list' aborted the run after the writer had already produced a full article. Prior run showed the writer's own malformed-output retry firing, so malformed output from these agents is routine, not exceptional.
bugs.root_cause: Resilience is unevenly distributed across stages that are equally prone to malformed LLM output. BUG-042 already established that the graphics call can need extra turns for its JSON, so the fragility was known for turns but not for content.
bugs.impact: Wastes the entire writer stage (~$0.85 and several minutes) on a graphics failure that a retry would likely absorb. Blocks B-020 acceptance.
bugs.proposed_fix: Give the graphics call the same bounded retry the writer has, feeding the ChartRenderError message back so the agent can correct the spec. Reuse the writer's attempt-loop shape rather than inventing a second one.
bugs.resolution: _graphics_with_retry in stage3_runner gives the graphics agent 3 bounded attempts, feeding ChartRenderError's own message back so it knows what to correct. Chart failures stay fatal, but 'fatal' now means 'no valid spec in 3 tries' rather than 'the first try was malformed'. Made async deliberately — a sync helper called from the async run_stage3 would have repeated the asyncio.run-inside-a-loop bug fixed the same day. Regression: tests/test_graphics_retry.py (3 tests). One existing test (test_run_stage3_fails_when_chart_render_fails) supplied only two mock replies so the retry hit StopIteration; its fixture was fixed, not its assertion.

bugs.description: _graphics_with_retry passes the FULL graphics_budget_usd to every attempt rather than the remaining balance, so _GRAPHICS_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 can spend up to 3x the cap the operator set. The writer loop decrements correctly (see BUG-061); graphics is the mirror-image inconsistency. Not a run-aborter — it silently overspends instead of under-funding. Measured graphics cost has already reached $0.41 against a $0.40 cap on one B-020 run (logs/agent_sdk_costs.jsonl 2026-07-28T01:22).
bugs.root_cause_notes: The graphics retry loop (BUG-063) was added after the writer loop and did not copy its cumulative-budget accounting.
bugs.discovered_by: code reading during the BUG-061 fix (B-021 slice 1)
bugs.fix_notes: _graphics_with_retry now hands each attempt graphics_budget_usd minus what earlier attempts spent, matching the writer loop. None (unbounded) stays unbounded rather than collapsing to 0.0.
bugs.verification: 3 regression tests + make ci-local green, 2380 passed (2026-07-28)

bugs.description: PRODUCTION ESCAPE. The <!-- HERO IMAGE - generate an image from the prompt below, then replace this whole comment with it --> block shipped into the published flaky-tests post and is still in the live page source (invisible in the render, but pipeline instructions on a public page). Two compounding causes: (1) pipeline._maybe_inject_hero_prompt injects the comment AFTER run_stage4, deliberately - 'Injected AFTER Stage 4 so validation is unchanged' - so the publication validator structurally CANNOT see it; (2) even if it could, _check_placeholders only matches TODO|FIXME|XXX|REPLACE_ME|YOUR_*, so a natural-language 'replace this whole comment' instruction is not placeholder text by its definition. The gate that exists for exactly this class of problem has a hole the pipeline drives through.
bugs.root_cause_notes: Injecting unpublishable content after the last gate that could reject it. The injection is correct in intent (the reviewer needs the brief when no hero was drawn); what is missing is any gate between injection and publish. Note B-016b/B-021 narrowed the blast radius - the comment is only injected when no hero is drawn, and Stage 3 now nearly always draws one - but the deploy path still cannot reject it.
bugs.discovered_by: manual review of the live post while regenerating the B-017 slop list
bugs.fix_notes: Gated at the DEPLOY boundary, not in publication_validator: the comment is injected after run_stage4 by design, so the validator cannot see it, and it is legitimate in the local artifact — only illegitimate on the blog. _reject_unrendered_hero_prompt guards BOTH deploy() and deploy_review() (a review deploy is a live URL too) and fires before any clone/push, so a rejected article costs nothing. Rejects rather than strips: stripping would hide that no hero was drawn. Removed from the live post in oviney/blog#1168.

bugs.root_cause_notes: claude_agent_sdk resolves its CLI as bundled-first: subprocess_cli._find_cli() returns _find_bundled_cli() before ever consulting shutil.which('claude'). This machine's .venv (Apr 3) pins the floor of requirements.txt's 'claude-agent-sdk>=0.1.68,<1.0.0', and 0.1.68 bundles Claude Code CLI 2.1.119 (Apr 25). That bundled binary is non-functional here - it hangs with no stderr and the SDK surfaces only 'Command failed with exit code 1 / Check stderr output for details'. The maintained system CLI at ~/.local/bin/claude (2.1.220) returns exit 0 on the identical stream-json invocation. Verified not a nesting artifact: the bundled binary still hangs with all CLAUDE*/ANTHROPIC* vars stripped. The wide version pin is what let one machine sit on a stale, broken SDK while the other machine (where B-020's five runs passed) runs a newer one.
bugs.discovered_by: article-two regeneration run aborted in seconds instead of the expected ~35 min
bugs.fix_notes: Raised the requirements.txt floor to claude-agent-sdk>=0.2.128 (bundles CLI 2.1.220, probed exit 0) and upgraded this machine's venv from 0.1.68. Fixed at the PIN, not with a cli_path override at the four ClaudeAgentOptions call sites: the SDK's bundled-first resolution is upstream behaviour, and the maintained fix is to stop permitting an SDK whose bundle is broken. Two guards: the declared floor cannot drift back below the known-good version (this is the RED reproduction - it failed on 0.1.68), and the INSTALLED sdk must satisfy that floor, so a stale venv fails at gate time instead of 35 minutes into a paid run. The second guard is the one that would actually have caught this incident.
bugs.verification: RED->GREEN on tests/test_agent_sdk_pin_contract.py (2 tests) + make ci-local green (2026-07-29)

bugs.root_cause_notes: claude_web catches every research failure and returns a findings-free brief (guardrail header only, 401 chars) so Stage 3 'degrades softly'. run_stage3 logs the char count and dispatches the writer with no emptiness check. The asymmetry is the defect: the deterministic provider path one line below (stage3_runner.py:668) raises EmptyResearchBriefError, and tests/test_empty_research_guard.py asserts run_stage3 propagates it. Two research paths, opposite failure policies, one silent. Not an oversight - the soft-degrade is documented in the docstring - so it needs a decision, not a patch. Measured: audit_article_stats against an empty brief is LEAKY, not absent - it stripped '84% of build failures' and 'a 21% drop' but kept 'the median pull request waits 4.3 hours', and cut 74 words to 47. Likely outcome is a word-count quarantine ~$1 into a run; tail risk is a published article carrying unsourced numbers.
bugs.discovered_by: reading the aborted article-two run log while diagnosing BUG-066
bugs.fix_notes: Implemented the owner-approved B-024 policy: fall back to the keyless deterministic providers, with abort underneath. Extracted the research block out of run_stage3 into _acquire_research_brief(topic, mode, override) -> (brief, cost, downgraded), which is the testable seam the old inline block never offered. Emptiness is detected with claude_web.brief_has_findings(), which compares against a freshly formatted empty brief rather than pattern-matching the header, so it cannot drift out of step with _format_brief. The failed leg's cost is carried forward rather than discarded, so the run report does not understate what the article cost. downgraded surfaces on Stage3Result.research_downgraded. KNOWN GAP: B-024 success criterion 3 says 'any --research-mode'; this covers claude_web (the defect) and deterministic (which already raised). 'deep' is NOT covered - it has its own duplicated _RESEARCH_BRIEF_GUARDRAILS and no equivalent predicate, and B-012 leaves it unexercised, so guarding it would mean shipping an untested path.
bugs.verification: RED->GREEN on tests/test_research_failure_fallback.py (4 tests); 26 research tests green

bugs.root_cause_notes: _CHROME_BINARIES = ('google-chrome', 'chromium', 'chromium-browser') is resolved with shutil.which(). On macOS - the owner's platform - Chrome ships as an app bundle at '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome' and is never on PATH under any of those three names, so which() always returns None. The hero render is skipped, and because the vision critique operates on the render, it is skipped too. The pipeline logs one WARNING and continues to a PASSED validator, so nothing downstream signals that the hero was never looked at. This defeats CLAUDE.md constraint #4 ('always look at the rendered result before shipping') on the very platform the owner runs, and it degrades silently rather than failing.
bugs.discovered_by: article-two run: hero drawn but never rendered; manual headless render showed the top card clipped
bugs.fix_notes: Extracted _find_chrome(): PATH first (an operator-installed binary is a deliberate choice and outranks a system default), then known app-bundle locations for macOS Chrome and Chromium. The skip warning now names every location searched and states plainly that nobody has looked at the hero. Also repaired test_missing_chrome_degrades_to_none_rather_than_raising, which patched only shutil.which and would have passed for the wrong reason on any Mac once bundle lookup existed.
bugs.verification: RED->GREEN on tests/test_hero_svg_chrome_discovery.py (4 tests); 40 hero tests green; _find_chrome() resolves the real bundle on this Mac

bugs.root_cause_notes: deploy() intended to stamp the deploy date onto the _posts filename - its own comment says 'Rename article file to today's deploy date' - but the mechanism was re.sub(r'^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-', f'{deploy_date}-', name), which REPLACES an existing date prefix and never ADDS one. Correct while the pipeline emitted dated files (output/2026-01-18-<slug>.md); B-006/B-008 moved generation to a canonical slug at output/posts/<slug>.md, undated, and the substitution silently became a no-op. The article would land at _posts/<slug>.md. Jekyll derives a post's date and URL from the filename (_config.yml: permalink /:year/:month/:day/:title/) and 0 of the blog's 26 posts are undated, so an undated file is not a publishable post.
bugs.discovered_by: reading the deploy dry-run output before opening the article PR
bugs.fix_notes: Extracted _dated_post_name(source_name, deploy_date): strip any existing YYYY-MM-DD- prefix, then always prefix the deploy date. Handles both shapes so the date cannot go missing again. WHY NO GATE CAUGHT IT, which is the more useful finding: scripts/validate-posts.sh globs _posts/*.md itself rather than asking Jekyll, so it validates an undated file happily; and acceptance_blog_frontmatter.sh stages its OWN copy as _posts/2026-01-01-<slug>.md - a different filename from the one the deploy path produces. The oracle passed on a name that would never exist. An oracle that renames its input is not testing the deploy path.
bugs.verification: RED->GREEN on tests/test_deploy_post_filename.py (3 tests); dry-run now targets _posts/2026-07-29-review-queue-throughput-tax.md

bugs.description: `make art` sets `image:` but never removes the `<!-- HERO IMAGE` prompt comment, so the documented B-042 sequence (draw hero -> make art -> deploy --mode review) is refused by _reject_unrendered_hero_prompt. The happy path cannot complete without an undocumented manual edit.
bugs.root_cause_notes: scripts/finalise_art.py calls pipeline._link_hero_asset, which edits only the frontmatter (image:, image_alt:). The body comment injected by pipeline._inject_hero_prompt_comment is left in place. Two gates written in different items (BUG-065's comment refusal, B-042's art hand-off) were never run against each other end to end; every unit test covers one or the other. Reproduced live 2026-08-02 with four deploy probes.

bugs.description: `## References` rendered as literal text on generated articles. The stat audit collapses the blank line before it; kramdown will not start a block element on the line after a paragraph. The CRITICAL inline_heading_marker check could not see it, because the same edit leaves a trailing space and the check's regex allowed only one whitespace character.
bugs.root_cause_notes:
audit_article_stats splits on (?<=[.!?])\s+ and rejoins with ' ', swallowing the newline before '## References'. This has happened on every article; Stage 4's unconditional chart embed sat in the gap and supplied the blank line by accident. B-042 deleted that embed, so the first chart-less article is the first one to break. Verified by running kramdown directly, and by the '.

## References' shape still on disk in both pre-B-042 articles.

bugs.description: `make art` crashed with UnicodeDecodeError on a real PNG hero. _hero_description called path.read_text() on any hero to harvest an SVG <desc>; a PNG is binary. .png is a first-class hero format (_HERO_SUFFIXES lists it, deploy generates its .webp sibling), so this was a supported path that had never been exercised.
bugs.root_cause_notes: PNG heroes in test_frontmatter_blog_contract.py are created with (images / 'my-slug-hero.png').write_text('stub') — a text file wearing a .png name — so read_text() always succeeded. Same class as BUG-070: the fixture is not what reality produces. Found by putting a real Gemini PNG on disk and running make art.
